High | Keys | audit_log | Table has no primary key | Rows have no guaranteed ID, so a row cannot be found, updated or linked reliably. | Add a primary key, for example on the id column.
Low | Speed | book(title) | Same index exists twice | Indexes ix_book_title and ix_book_title_again cover the same columns. The extra one only slows down writes. | Drop one of them.
Medium | Duplicates | book.isbn | Identifier can be duplicated | isbn is the kind of value that should identify one record, but the database allows the same value twice. | Check for duplicates, then add a unique rule on isbn.
Medium | Consistency | book: summary_xml, summary_json | Same data saved in several formats | The same information is saved 2 times in different formats. If the copies disagree, nobody knows which one is right. | Decide which format is the master copy and compare the others with it before migrating.
Low | Naming | loan.book_id → book_copy | Column name suggests a different table | The column is called book_id, which sounds like a link to book, but it links to book_copy. It works, but it confuses people and import scripts. | Rename the column or document the link in a column comment.
High | Links | loan.member_id → member | Link rule was never checked for older rows | The rule "every member_id must exist in member" was added with NOT VALID. New rows are checked, but rows that already existed were never checked and may point to nothing. | Count the rows that break the rule. If there are none, run: ALTER TABLE public.loan VALIDATE CONSTRAINT "Loan Member";
Low | Speed | loan: book_id | A link has no index | Joins over these links and deletes of the linked rows get slow as the table grows. | Add an index on book_id.
Medium | Links | loan.external_ref | Looks like a link, but nothing checks it | external_ref seems to hold the ID of another record, but there is no rule (foreign key). It can point to records that do not exist. | Count values with no matching record. If the link is real, add a foreign key.
Low | Speed | loan_item: book_id | A link has no index | Joins over these links and deletes of the linked rows get slow as the table grows. | Add an index on book_id.
Medium | Keys | loan_item.id | Extra id column is not unique | The real key is (loan_id, book_id). There is also an id column, but nothing stops two rows from having the same id. | Make id unique, or do not use it as an identifier.
High | Security | member.password | Sensitive data | This column looks like it stores passwords. It must never be copied to another system. | Exclude it from every export and import. Check that values are hashed.
High | Security | member.api_token | Sensitive data | This column looks like it stores secrets. It must never be copied to another system. | Exclude it from every export and import. Check that values are hashed.
Low | Links | member.favourite_ids | List of IDs cannot be checked | favourite_ids stores several IDs in one field. The database cannot check that they exist, so deleted records stay listed. | Use a link table (one row per ID) if these lists matter.
Low | Duplicates | member.email | Unique column may be empty | email must be unique, but it can also be left empty, and empty values do not count as duplicates. | Make it required if every row needs one.
Medium | Time | member | Two kinds of time in one table | Some time columns store a time zone and some do not. It is like writing one time in local time and another in UTC. | Use timestamp with time zone everywhere, or document which zone the others use.
Medium | Links | branch_code in loan, member | Shared code with no lookup list | branch_code appears in 2 tables as a plain number. There is no table that lists the allowed values, so wrong or empty values are possible. It also has different types: integer / smallint. | Create a small lookup table of valid branch_code values and link to it.
Low | Naming | loan.order, member.user | Names that need quotes in SQL | These names are reserved words in SQL. Every query must write them in double quotes, which is easy to forget. | Rename them when convenient, or always quote them.
Low | Naming | branch: primary key named fk_branch; loan: link named pk_loan_book | Misleading rule names | Some primary keys are named like links (fk…) or links are named like primary keys (pk…). | Rename the rules so the name matches what they do.
Low | Keys | uuid_generate_v4, gen_random_uuid | Different ID generators | Tables create their IDs with different functions. It works, but IDs sort differently from table to table. | Pick one generator for new tables.
Info | Content | audit_log, book, book_copy, loan, loan_item, member | Row counts unknown | The database has never collected statistics for these tables, so their size is unknown. They are probably empty. | Run ANALYZE, or count the rows.
Low | Descriptions | 0 of 7 tables, 1 of 29 columns | Descriptions on 3% of columns | Few columns explain what they mean. People have to guess, and matching with another database gets harder. | Add COMMENT ON COLUMN for the important columns, starting with the ones you migrate.
